question: A 55-year-old male tobacco smoker presents with a six-month history of hoarseness. Laryngoscopy shows a superficial lesion confined to the right vocal cord with normal cord mobility. A second patient of the same age with the same smoking history presents with a three-week history of a painless neck lump; laryngoscopy shows a lesion of the aryepiglottic fold. Which explanation BEST accounts for why the second patient presented later with nodal disease while the first presented early with hoarseness?

answers.text: The glottis has sparse lymphatics and any lesion causes early hoarseness by disrupting vocal fold vibration, whereas the supraglottis has a rich lymphatic supply and does not produce hoarseness until late.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This is the essential glottic vs supraglottic distinction. Glottic carcinoma causes early hoarseness (even T1 lesions disturb vibration) and has sparse lymphatics so nodal spread is late; supraglottic carcinoma is clinically silent until advanced, but its rich lymphatic drainage leads to early bilateral neck node metastasis.

answers.text: Supraglottic tumours are more aggressive histologically (adenocarcinoma vs squamous cell carcinoma) and therefore spread faster.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Both glottic and supraglottic carcinomas are overwhelmingly squamous cell carcinomas (>95%). The difference in nodal spread is anatomical — lymphatic density — not histological aggressiveness.

answers.text: Glottic carcinomas are more vascular and therefore bleed earlier, prompting the patient to seek attention before nodal disease develops.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Glottic carcinomas present early because even small lesions disrupt the vibratory mucosal wave and cause hoarseness — not because of bleeding. The key is the early symptom of voice change, not haemorrhage.

answers.text: The supraglottis lies above the cricoid and therefore drains to the upper deep cervical nodes, which are larger and more easily palpable.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While it is true that supraglottic drainage is to upper deep cervical nodes, this does not explain the difference in symptom timing. The correct explanation is that the glottis gives early symptoms via hoarseness and has sparse lymphatics, while the supraglottis is clinically silent with rich bilateral lymphatics.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the lymphatic drainage and symptom profile of glottic versus supraglottic carcinoma. The key: glottis has sparse lymphatics and causes hoarseness early; supraglottis has rich bilateral lymphatics and is clinically silent until late.

Excellent. The glottic vs supraglottic distinction is a board favourite: glottic = early hoarseness, late nodes, better prognosis; supraglottic = late presentation, early bilateral nodes, worse prognosis.
